title: A decimal integer of 4300 digits is exact or refused
notes: The Core schema reads a plain scalar that matches `[-+]?[0-9]+` as an integer and gives that pattern no upper bound (section 10.3.2). YAML 1.2.2 section 10.2.1.3 lets a processor reject an integer it cannot hold as an error. The kit therefore accepts the exact integer or a refusal (strict: a `limit` error). Truncating or converting the value fails, because the kit cannot see a warning. A crash, a hang, a wrong result, or more than the stated time or memory fails. The resource bounds are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. 4300 digits is the largest integer the kit's own JSON reader converts, so it is the largest one a case can state as a value; longer scalars are covered as events (`safety/ten-million-digit-plain-scalar-events`). Converting a long digit string to an integer takes more than linear time in some runtimes, which is why a digit cap with a limit error is a reasonable answer.
